````math
^(a) Inference-time results on frozen weights are a separate class and
are not rank-comparable with trained rows; the honest figure is the
within-model (w.m.) delta against the filter-off control.
^(b) Checkpoint selected by composite on the scoring densities; the
audit quantifies the selection optimism at about $`1.9`$ points.
^(c) The winning reward-scale arm trained for more steps than its
siblings; the gain is step-confounded and overlaps the anchor CI.
^(d) Hybrid and tuning batches reference the cross-stream champion (the
batch-1 DAgger control arm, $`87.28`$) once it existed; earlier batches
reference their paradigm anchor. “Tie” marks CI-overlapping results.
^(e) This stream pre-registered an OOD-retention ratio $`R`$ (success on
the out-of-distribution densities relative to in-distribution success)
as its metric; its falsification bar is on $`R`$, not the composite.

## Appendix D Implementation Details

### D.1 Environment Specification

Table [10](#A4.T10 "Table 10 ‣ D.1 Environment Specification ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details ‣ An AI Scientist that Doesn’t Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop")
summarizes the simulation environment parameters. All experiments use
the environment implemented in MuJoCo ([Todorov et al.,
2012](#bib.bib10)) with GPU acceleration via the MJX framework ([Freeman
et al., 2021](#bib.bib6)). We use LiDAR rather than RGB because MJX
supports efficient ray-based sensing in JAX while parallel RGB rendering
is unsupported. Episodes terminate on goal reach (within
$`0.5\,\mathrm{m}`$), collision, fall, or timeout.

|                            |                                  |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Parameter                  | Value                            |
| Environment                | Go1NavigationForestEnvV5         |
| Training room              | 30m $`\times`$ 30m               |
| Control frequency          | 50 Hz                            |
| Episode length             | 3,000 steps (60s)                |
| Goal threshold             | 0.5m                             |
| Robot radius               | 0.3m                             |
| Obstacle density           | 0.04 trees/m²                    |
| Obstacle radius            | 0.3m                             |
| LiDAR beams                | 64                               |
| LiDAR range                | 10m                              |
| $`v_{x}`$ range            | $`[0,\,1.5]\,\mathrm{m/s}`$      |
| $`v_{y}`$ range            | $`[-0.6,\,0.6]\,\mathrm{m/s}`$   |
| $`v_{\mathrm{yaw}}`$ range | $`[-1.2,\,1.2]\,\mathrm{rad/s}`$ |

Table 10: Environment parameters.

### D.2 Observation Space

Table [11](#A4.T11 "Table 11 ‣ D.2 Observation Space ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details ‣ An AI Scientist that Doesn’t Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop")
details the observation space components (75D total). The encoding
deliberately omits absolute position so the policy is scale-invariant to
room size.

| Component | Dims |  Description |
|----|----|----|
| Normalized goal distance | 1 |  $`\mathrm{clip}(d_{\mathrm{goal}}/D_{0},\,0,\,1)`$, $`D_{0}=30\sqrt{2}`$ m |
| Normalized heading-to-goal | 1 |  Heading-to-goal difference, mapped to $`[-1,1]`$ |
| LiDAR | 64 |  Normalized 360^(∘) ring, $`[0,1]`$ |
| Action history | 9 |  Flattened previous-3 velocity commands $`(v_{x},v_{y},v_{\mathrm{yaw}})`$ |

Table 11: Observation space components (75D total).

### D.3 Data Collection

Expert demonstrations are collected using A\* ([Hart et al.,
1968](#bib.bib11)) planning on an inflated occupancy grid (0.2m
resolution) with Pure Pursuit ([Coulter, 1992](#bib.bib9)) tracking
(3.0m lookahead). The expert has access to the complete obstacle map:
privileged information unavailable to the student during deployment. We
collect $`{\sim}8.65`$M expert transitions, shared by the PIL and
offline-RL paradigms.

### D.4 Computational Resources

Experiments ran on a shared cluster, predominantly on NVIDIA H200 and
L40S GPUs, using the JAX/Flax framework with MJX simulation. PIL methods
train in under 2 hours, IQL requires approximately 4 hours, and PPO
requires approximately 6 hours with 512 parallel environments.

## Appendix E The Program Description

Both arms read the same program description at every step: it is the one
document every subagent shares, and in the without-kkanbu arm it is the
only source of direction. We reproduce it below in full, as the agents
read it. Local context is masked as \<...\>: cluster-specific filesystem
paths, the frozen locomotion checkpoint identifier, and the oracle
profile’s install path. Internal codenames are kept so the document
stays authentic; the glossary: *Round 5* is the run this paper reports;
*R1–R4* are earlier development runs whose numerical findings the
document excludes by rule; *round5b* is the without-kkanbu arm;
*d06–d11* are the six discovery streams (Hybrid I/II, New-paradigm I/II,
Tuning I/II of
Appendix [C](#A3 "Appendix C Per-Experiment Results ‣ An AI Scientist that Doesn’t Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop"));
*ADR $`n`$* cites an internal architecture-decision record; *V5* is the
fifth revision of the observation space (the document’s §13.4 gives the
lineage); SLURM is the cluster’s job scheduler.

Two passages are superseded by how the ablation actually ran. The
document’s §1 and §7 lock a *planned* without-oracle arm in which a
static digest of the taste profile is pasted into the subagent prompts.
That digest was never built: the arm as run consulted no taste artifact
at all
(Section [4.5](#S4.SS5 "4.5 Isolating kkanbu: a controlled ablation ‣ 4 The AI Scientist System ‣ An AI Scientist that Doesn’t Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop")),
so the measured contrast is live oracle versus no oracle, not live
retrieval versus a static digest of the same taste.

[⬇](data:text/plain;base64,)

\# Autoresearch Round 5 -- Program

\> Universal guideline for every agent in Round 5. This document
answers: what we are trying

\> to do, how the problem is measured, what is allowed to change, and
who

\> does what.

---

\## 1. Goal

Find \*\*genuine experiments\*\* that improve understanding of density

generalization in quadruped navigation, under a clean V5 baseline. The

deliverable is understanding -- evidence that survives transfer between
methods.

A higher composite score is the \*test\* of that understanding, not the
goal.

An experiment is \*genuine\* if, whether it succeeds or fails, we learn

something about why policies generalize (or fail to) across densities.

An experiment is \*\*not\*\* genuine if it is a local-optimum tuning
that

tells us nothing beyond "X% more at delta = 0.04."

Round 5 is a \*\*clean-slate re-instantiation\*\* of the autoresearch
program.

No numerical findings, calibrated leaders, or single-seed claims from
R1-R4

carry over (codebase improvements, methods, and the eval protocol do).

Round 5 establishes its own anchors via a human-seeded batch 0 where
provided, else the paradigm streams' batch-1.

A separate later run (\*\*round5b\*\*) will mirror Round 5 with kkanbu
replaced

by a generic LLM (same prompt scaffolding) to produce the camera-ready

ablation comparison. Round 5 must therefore be \*reproducible by a
different

oracle running the same protocol\*.

---

\## 2. Score system

Policies are trained at obstacle density \*\*delta = 0.04 trees/m^2\*\*
on a

30x30 m forest and evaluated across six densities:

\| delta \| 0.01 \| 0.02 \| 0.04 \| 0.08 \| 0.12 \| 0.16 \|

\|---\|---\|---\|---\|---\|---\|---\|

\| weight \| 1.0 \| 1.0 \| 1.0 \| 1.5 \| 2.0 \| 2.5 \|

The \*\*composite score\*\* is the weighted average of success rates
(divisor 9.0).

Weighting OOD densities (delta \> 0.04) more heavily makes the metric
reward

out-of-distribution survival over in-distribution fit.

Computed with \`\<run-root\>/tools/compute_composite_score.py\`.

\*\*Eval determinism floor (R3 finding, carried forward)\*\*: identical
reruns

of the same checkpoint drift by +/-1.4 pp on the composite score.
\*\*This

must be verified below +/-0.3 pp before the streams launch\*\* (see S8
G1) -- and

fixed if it isn't. Until the drift is below +/-0.3 pp, no sub-2 pp claim
is

real signal. Multi-seed

\*\*mean +/- stratified percentile bootstrap 95% CI\*\* is the canonical
reporting

form (NOT IQM; IQM(n=3) degenerates to median).

---

\## 3. What we're starting from

Round 5 inherits the codebase, the locomotion checkpoint, the methods

implementations, and the eval protocol. It does \*\*not\*\* inherit:

- Numerical leaders, anchor values, or named findings from R1-R4

- Calibrated benchmarks (the R3 leaders B1-E6, B1-E4, R2-B4-C9 are
\*not\*

reference points for Round 5)

- The Without-kkanbu n=50 ablation data (the old loop architecture is
gone)

- Single-seed claims from any prior round

Each paradigm stream's anchor is established by its \*\*human-seeded
batch 0\*\*

where one is provided (the best manually-tuned policy for that stream),
and

otherwise by its \*\*batch-1\*\* default-config run (S4.5). A batch-0
anchor, once

written, is not overwritten by batch-1.

The kkanbu graph state on the cluster \*may\* contain references to old

findings (R1-R4 may have used \`learn=True\` before the R4 mandate).
This

is to be inspected (S8 G2) and pruned if contaminated.

---

\## 4. Structure

\### 4.1 The 11-stream / 4-batch layout (no phases)

Round 5 has \*\*11 streams\*\*, each advancing through \*\*4
batches\*\*. All 11

streams run \*\*in parallel from t=0\*\*; there are \*\*no phases\*\*
(ADR 0012).

Total: 44 experiments. Concurrency is \<=11 experiments in flight (one
batch

per stream).

\| Stream \| Name \| Class \| Specificity \|

\|---\|---\|---\|---\|

\| 1 \| \`pure_rl\` \| paradigm \| Paradigm fixed (was "online_rl") \|

\| 2 \| \`privileged_rl\` \| paradigm \| Paradigm fixed \|

\| 3 \| \`offline_rl\` \| paradigm \| Paradigm fixed \|

\| 4 \| \`pil_control\` \| paradigm \| Paradigm fixed \|

\| 5 \| \`pil_trajectory\` \| paradigm \| Paradigm fixed \|

\| 6 \| \`d06\` \| hybrid \| kkanbu picks freely (combination /
improvement) \|

\| 7 \| \`d07\` \| hybrid \| kkanbu picks freely (combination /
improvement) \|

\| 8 \| \`d08\` \| new \| kkanbu picks freely (totally new idea) \|

\| 9 \| \`d09\` \| new \| kkanbu picks freely (totally new idea) \|

\| 10 \| \`d10\` \| tuning \| kkanbu picks freely (minor tuning within
constraint) \|

\| 11 \| \`d11\` \| tuning \| kkanbu picks freely (minor tuning within
constraint) \|

Subdirs under \`\<run-root\>/experiment_cards/\`,

\`\<run-root\>/brainstormer/\`, etc., use these names. Streams 6-11

should rename their subdir from \`d\##/\` to \`d\##\_\<topic\>/\` once
kkanbu

commits to a topic in the stream's batch 1.

\### 4.2 Parallel execution (no phases)

All 11 streams run \*\*in parallel from t=0\*\* (ADR 0012). There is no
phase

ordering and no cross-stream barrier. Stream \*roles\* still differ:

- \*\*Paradigm\*\* (streams 1-5): paradigm-incremental, mechanism-aware.

Establish the per-stream anchors (S4.5).

- \*\*Hybrid\*\* (streams 6-7): cross-paradigm combinations /
improvements.

At t=0 no sibling results exist yet, so \*\*batch-1 designs from
\*paradigm

priors\*\*\* -- the S12 paradigm definitions and known mechanisms, not
this

round's numbers. \*\*Later batches fold in\*\* whatever sibling cards
are

\`complete\` by then, designing from those actual results. (Same "start
from

priors, refine as the leaderboard fills in" pattern as tuning, S12.7.)

- \*\*New\*\* (streams 8-9): paradigm discovery, novel architectures.

Anchorless; start immediately.

- \*\*Tuning\*\* (streams 10-11): batch-1 tunes a fixed baseline
paradigm

assigned upfront (S4.5, S12.7); later batches re-target the current

champion (highest-composite \`complete\` card across all streams).

A stream's \*\*batch\*\* is \`complete\` when card parts 1-7 are written
and the

3-seed eval is finalized; \`skipped\` when any S4.6 cap is hit (5 ALGO

attempts, 3 code-reviewer FAILs, or kkanbu-proposed skip). Both are

\*\*terminal\*\*. No stream waits on any other stream.

\### 4.3 Batches (per-stream sequential)

Batches advance \*\*independently per stream\*\*. Batch N+1 of a stream
starts

as soon as \*that stream's\* batch N reaches terminal status -- it does
\*\*not\*\*

wait for any other stream (ADR 0012). The brainstormer for batch N+1
sees

whatever sibling cards are \`complete\` at that moment (an opportunistic

snapshot, not a synchronized set). This trades cross-stream batch
context

for wall-clock; the loss is recovered as later batches consume more

completed siblings.

\*\*Stream abandonment\*\*: if \*\*3 consecutive batches\*\* in the same
stream

are skipped (for any cause -- SLURM ALGO cap, code-reviewer FAIL cap, or

kkanbu dry brainstorm), the stream is \*\*abandoned\*\* (no future
batches run

for it). The maintainer detects this and writes

\`state/streams/{stream}.json\` with \`status: "abandoned"\`. Because
streams

no longer synchronize, an abandoned stream simply stops -- there is no

barrier to release. Cap configurable via

\`project.yaml caps.consecutive_skips_for_stream_abandonment\` (default
3).

\### 4.4 Multi-seed protocol

Every Round 5 experiment uses \*\*3 seeds via the staged 1+2
protocol\*\*.

There are NO exceptions -- anchor calibration (the 5 paradigm streams,

batch-1) follows the same flow.

1. \*\*Seed 1 (debug)\*\*: builder generates parameterized scripts; the

code-reviewer gates between builder and submit; orchestrator launches

\`submit.sh\`. Debugger fixes any infra/code issues. Most bugs surface
here

without spending 3x the seeds.

2. \*\*Seeds 2 & 3 (calibration)\*\*: only launched after seed 1's
training +

eval succeed AND seed 1 is \*\*not cratered\*\*. "Cratered" is defined
as:

 - Training crashed (NaN, divergence, OOM with no recovery), OR

 - Composite \< \`project.yaml seed_protocol.cratered_threshold_pct\`
(default 10%

absolute -- below the dumbest baseline), OR

 - For d08-d09 paradigm-discovery slots: the hypothesis was clearly

falsified at single-seed level.

When seeds 2+3 launch, the initial-analyzer re-runs after all 3 seeds

complete and reports composite in the canonical form (S2).

No single-seed claim is reportable. Single-seed-only is acceptable for

paradigm-discovery / feasibility checks in streams 8-9 (cratered or

borderline seed-1 results, or \`totally_new\` slots that need to fail
fast),

explicitly justified in the card's part-5 analysis.

\*\*Human-seeded batch 0 (S4.5) is an explicit exception to the
\*reportability\*

rule, not to the protocol.\*\* A batch-0 anchor may be \`single_seed\`
-- it is a

provisional baseline-to-beat, not a reported claim. The reportable
result for a

paradigm stream is its \*\*batch-1\*\* experiment, which runs the full
1+2 protocol

\*and modifies the batch-0 recipe\* (S4.5): batch-1 restores 3-seed
rigor by trying

to improve on the human baseline, scored against the batch-0 anchor.

\> The earlier "within ~5pp of anchor" gate was dropped (Q7 grilling
resolution):

\> the most interesting cases -- big improvements or big regressions --
are

\> exactly what we want to verify with more seeds. The gate now protects

\> against compute waste on cratered runs only.

\### 4.5 Anchor benchmarks

Round 5 inherits no \*numerical\* anchors from R1-R4, but each paradigm
stream

\*\*may be human-seeded with a batch 0\*\*: the best manually-tuned
policy for that

stream, recorded as \`state/anchors/{stream}.json\` (the
baseline-to-beat). Where

a stream has no batch 0, its \*\*batch-1\*\* establishes the anchor by
running the

paradigm at default config through the \*\*standard 1+2 seed
protocol\*\* (per S4.4).

A human-seeded batch-0 anchor is never overwritten by batch-1 (see

\`experiment-initial-analyzer S3b\`). Batch-0 anchors may be
\`single_seed\` and/or

\`provisional\` (fewer than 6 densities present).

\*\*A \`provisional: true\` anchor is NOT a valid numeric comparison
threshold.\*\* Its

\`composite_weighted\` is computed on an incomplete denominator
(\`densities_present\`),

so ranking a full 6-density result against it would mis-classify
improvements and

regressions. Enforced rule -- \*provisional falls back to the
falsification clause\*:

- The provisional anchor's \*\*own\*\* paradigm stream judges each batch
against the

card's \`expected_falsification\` clause, \*\*not\*\* a composite Delta
.

- \*\*Derived streams treat a provisional referenced anchor as
\*unavailable\*\*\*, the

same as an abandoned stream: drop it from \`max(referenced means)\`, and
if every

reference is provisional/abandoned the slot goes anchorless (the
falsification

clause carries the bar).

The numeric anchor becomes usable only once a complete 6-density value
replaces it

(the queued re-evals -- \`state/batch0_handoff_runbook.md\`). This rule
is enforced

by guards in \`experiment-initial-analyzer S2e\`,
\`experiment-mechanism-analyzer

S1f\`, and the \`brainstormer\` anchor-reference selection (it amends
the ADR 0009

policy: a referenced anchor must be non-provisional to be used
numerically).

\*\*Batch-1 of a paradigm stream that has a human-seeded batch 0 does
not run a

from-scratch default\*\* -- instead the brainstormer proposes a
\*\*modification /

improvement of the batch-0 recipe\*\* (reading the batch-0 card's
\`3\_description\`

config and mutating it) and runs it under the full 1+2 seed protocol,
scored

against the batch-0 anchor. This is how a single-seed human baseline is
both

\*kept\* as the bar and \*superseded\* by a reportable 3-seed result.
(Streams with

no batch 0 fall back to the default-config batch-1 calibration above.)

When the \`experiment-initial-analyzer\` aggregates a batch-1's 3-seed
results for

a paradigm stream without a batch-0 anchor, it writes
\`state/anchors/{stream}.json\`

with the canonical mean +/- CI (S2). That value is the stream's anchor
for the

remainder of Round 5. Anchors are a \*\*scoring\*\* input, not a
scheduling gate

(ADR 0012): derived streams consume them whenever they land -- no stream
waits.

Subsequent batches reference \*their own stream's\* anchor (not a

cross-paradigm leader). This matches the project's "we don't want a
single

leader to bias the search" stance.

Derived streams (hybrid / new / tuning) have \*\*no separate anchor JSON
of

their own\*\*. Their "interesting threshold" is governed by

\`card.anchor_reference\`, which the brainstormer fixes at slot-design
time

and records in card part 1. Per-stream-class policy:

\| Stream class \| \`anchor_reference\` \| Threshold \|

\|---\|---\|---\|

\| Paradigm (streams 1-5) \| implicit / omitted \| own stream's
\`state/anchors/{stream}.json\` \|

\| \`d06\`, \`d07\` (hybrid) \| list of 1-2 paradigm stream names \|
\`max(referenced anchor means)\` over \*\*non-provisional,
non-abandoned\*\* references; anchorless (falsification clause) if none
remain \|

\| \`d08\`, \`d09\` (totally new) \| \`null\` \|
\`expected_falsification\` clause from card part 4 \|

\| \`d10\`, \`d11\` (tuning) \| card_id -- batch-1: the assigned
paradigm's batch-0 card where present, else its batch-1 card; later: the
current champion card \| batch-1: that paradigm's anchor; later:
champion card's composite (mean +/- CI) \|

If a referenced paradigm stream is abandoned (S4.3's 3-skip rule),

the next batch's brainstormer re-picks \`anchor_reference\` using
surviving

streams. If all references in a 2-list are abandoned, the slot goes

anchorless (\`null\`) and card part 3 records the cascade with the

\`expected_falsification\` clause carrying the bar.

\### 4.6 Skip rule

\*\*Failure classification.\*\* Every debugger invocation appends a
debug note

with one of two classifications:

- \*\*ALGO\*\* -- the experiment's own code/config/algorithm is at
fault. The

debugger fixed (or attempted to fix) something inside the experiment:

a config typo, a wrong import, a tensor shape mismatch, a loss that

diverges, a checkpoint-restore bug, a misused framework API. These are

attributable to the experiment.

- \*\*INFRA\*\* -- the experiment's code is fine; the cluster
misbehaved. Node

died, NFS hiccup, SLURM transient error, GPU evicted, OOM caused by a

noisy neighbor on the node, JAX/CUDA install drift on the runner. These

are \*not\* attributable to the experiment.

\*\*Skip threshold.\*\* After \*\*5 ALGO-classified debugger
attempts\*\* on a

single slot, mark \`status: skipped\` with \`reopen_candidate: true\`.

INFRA-classified attempts do \*\*NOT\*\* count toward the threshold
(retry

freely on infrastructure problems).

A skipped batch is terminal, so the stream's next batch proceeds (there
is

no synchronization to wait on -- ADR 0012). The next batch's
brainstormer

for that stream sees the skipped slot in its prior-cards context and
asks

kkanbu whether to retry under eased conditions.

Lowered from R4's 10-attempt threshold: R3/R4 distributions show most

real fixes resolve in 1-3 attempts; 5 still allows for a hairy initial

debug period without burning compute on fundamentally stuck slots.

\*\*Code-reviewer FAIL cap\*\*: 3 consecutive review-FAILs on a

single slot -\> slot \`skipped\` with \`reopen_candidate: true\`.
\*\*Separate

counter\*\* from the SLURM ALGO cap -- different failure classes have

different roots (review-FAIL -\> card ambiguity or constraint violation;

SLURM ALGO -\> runtime code bug). Cap configurable via

\`project.yaml caps.review_fail_attempts\` (default 3).

---

\## 5. Fair-comparison rules

\### What CAN be changed (freely, unless the card says otherwise)

- \*\*Training paradigm\*\* (within stream's allowed scope) -- pure RL,

privileged RL, offline RL (IQL / CQL / TD3+BC / AWR), PIL Control,

PIL Trajectory, paradigm hybrids, or a genuinely new paradigm.

- \*\*Network architecture around the core MLP\*\* -- attention
branches,

action-history encoders, density-conditioning heads. The core MLP

hidden sizes (512, 256, 128) are immutable; auxiliary modules around

it are free.

- \*\*Observation space\*\* -- add/remove features; change encodings;

change action-history length (\`action_history_len in {0,1,2,3}\` -- the

number \*k\* of previous actions in the observation; \*\*R5 default
k=1\*\*,

per the H1 action-history ablation; kkanbu-available to

\*\*every paradigm/stream\*\*). For RL paradigms (\`pure_rl\`,

\`privileged_rl\`) the obs and network input auto-adapt to k; these may

revert to k=3 if PPO jerkiness returns (S13.6). For data-driven

paradigms (\`offline_rl\`, \`pil_control\`, \`pil_trajectory\`) the demo

dataset for any k \<= 3 is obtained by \*\*slicing the canonical k=3 /
75D

bundle -- no re-collection\*\*: keep \`obs\[:66\]\` (base + LIDAR) plus
the

last \`3k\` dims (\`obs\[75-3k:75\]\`, the k most-recent actions), which

matches what the env emits at \`action_history_len=k\`

(\`tools/slice_obs_to_hist1.py\` produces the k=1 file). obs dim =

\`2 + num_beams + 3k\`; the student/policy net input layer auto-adapts
--

there is no hardcoded 75D. Note: the shipped env/training configs still

set \`action_history_len=3\` (preserving k=3 reproducibility); a stream

realizes the k=1 default by setting it explicitly in its config. Also:

change normalization.

- \*\*Action-history length is a per-stream knob for all 5 paradigm
streams\*\*

(pure_rl, privileged_rl, offline_rl, pil_control, pil_trajectory). A
stream's

batch-0 anchor may use a different action-history dim (hence obs dim)
than its

later experiments; the anchor is compared as a composite number, not by
obs dim.

- \*\*Reward structure (RL only)\*\* -- shaping terms, collision
weighting,

curricula. \`velocity_smoothness_scale\` is a kkanbu-available knob.

- \*\*Control-side parameters\*\* -- MAF, Pure-Pursuit
\`lookahead_index\`,

trajectory horizon.

- \*\*Hyperparameters\*\* -- learning rate, batch size, schedule,
warmup.

- \*\*Data\*\* -- regenerate for new observation or expert variants when
an

experiment explicitly requires it. Do not regenerate gratuitously.

- \*\*Analysis tools\*\* -- new Python scripts go under

\`\<run-root\>/tools/\`, authored on demand by the
\`mechanism-analyzer\`.

Each analysis script must finish in \*\*\<=20 min wall-clock\*\*
(R4-inherited cap,

\`project.yaml budgets.analysis_tool_runtime_max_min\`); exceed it -\>
subsample

or use cached eval outputs. The cap is enforced by a \`timeout\` wrapper
in the

analyzer subagent prompts (operational detail per S11). R4's \`tools/\`
is the

starting set (in practice just \`compute_composite_score.py\`).

\### What CANNOT be changed (immutable)

- \*\*Perception modality\*\*: LIDAR only. No depth, no camera.

- \*\*Locomotion layer\*\*: frozen. Reference by absolute path

\`\<frozen-locomotion-checkpoint\>\`.

- \*\*Environment fundamentals\*\*: physics, 30x30 m room, obstacle
generation

logic.

- \*\*Evaluation pipeline\*\*: the six-density sweep with the fixed
composite

weighting. Only the target density varies.

- \*\*Training data scale\*\*: keep roughly the same order of magnitude
of

demonstrations (10k-scale, not 10x more).

- \*\*Sim-to-real\*\*: out of scope.

- \*\*Network hidden sizes for the core policy MLP\*\*: \`(512, 256,
128)\`.

Non-negotiable. Auxiliary modules around the core MLP may have their

own dimensionalities -- those are free.

- \*\*Env\*\*: \`Go1NavigationForestEnvV5\` is the round-5 standard.

\`Go1NavigationForestEnvV3\` is registered for code-history reasons but

\*\*not used in any Round 5 experiment\*\*.

- \*\*Training distribution is fixed throughout training (no curriculum

learning).\*\* The training-time obstacle density (delta=0.04), room
size

(30x30 m), obstacle generation parameters, reward weights, and goal

distribution must not vary across training steps within a single run.

Optimization-side schedules (LR, warmup, batch size, exploration noise

/ entropy coefficient) are permitted -- these are not curriculum.

\### Tuning (streams 10-11) defined by negation

"No new losses, no new paradigms, no architectural changes. Network core

immutable. Any other hyperparameter is fair."

Batch-1 of each tuning stream grinds a fixed baseline paradigm assigned

upfront; later batches re-target the current champion (S4.5, S12.7).

Streams 10 and 11 may share or diverge on their target.

---

\## 6. Who is who

\*\*Orchestrator\*\* -- the persistent Claude session that runs the
per-stream

flows in parallel, dispatches subagents, tracks per-stream state in

memory, and reads \`state/{stream}/\*.txt\` files for continuity across

cron wakes. It does not itself read literature, pick experiments, or

edit code.

\*\*Crons\*\* -- Cron \#1 nudges the orchestrator ("for each stream,
where are

you in the flow?"); Cron \#2 runs the maintainer subagent. Intervals
live in

\`project.yaml crons\` (defaults: nudge every 10 min, maintainer every
20 min).

Both are launched as a setup step before the streams launch (S8 G4) and
run

until Round 5 completes. Crons do not drive the flow; they only pulse.

\*\*Subagents (10)\*\* -- each has one narrow role:

\| Subagent \| Role \| Calls kkanbu? \|

\|---\|---\|---\|

\| \`advisor-consult\` \| kkanbu wrapper. Ad-hoc; not in the per-stream
pipeline. \| Yes (its purpose) \|

\| \`websearcher\` \| Iterative web search for a single stream's batch,
directed by kkanbu (\`learn=False\`). \| Yes \|

\| \`brainstormer\` \| Packages per-stream context (websearch + prior
cards across all streams + relevant resource docs) and relays to kkanbu
(\`learn=False\`), which designs the slot for that stream's batch. \|
Yes \|

\| \`experiment-starter\` \| Transcribes a slot proposal into card parts
1-4 and creates the git worktree on the \`lite_round5\` branch. \| No \|

\| \`experiment-builder\` \| Implements the experiment inside the
worktree. One atomic commit per build. \| No \|

\| \`experiment-debugger\` \| Fixes SLURM failures. 5 ALGO attempts
before auto-skip (see S4.6 for ALGO vs INFRA definitions). \| No \|

\| \`experiment-initial-analyzer\` \| Populates card part 5 (training
curves, eval scores). Writes \`state/anchors/{stream}.json\` for the 5
paradigm streams' batch-1 (S4.5). \| No \|

\| \`experiment-mechanism-analyzer\` \| Redoes analysis per kkanbu's
probe request (\`learn=False\`). May write a reusable tool under
\`\<run-root\>/tools/\`. Populates card parts 6 and 7. \*\*Sees only own
stream's history mid-batch.\*\* \| Yes (3 probe turns + register turn)
\|

\| \`maintainer\` \| Walks cards across all 11 stream subdirs and SLURM
queue. Updates \`index.md\` (incl. the cross-stream champion for
\`d10\`/\`d11\`, S12.7). Writes status deltas. Tracks per-stream batch
progress. \| No \|

\| \`code-reviewer\` (new) \| Reviews builder commit before SLURM
submit. Returns PASS / SUGGEST / FAIL. Card status moves to
\`reviewed\_\*\`. \| No \|

\*\*kkanbu\*\* -- a local MCP advisor (profile \`scientist\`,
repo-frozen snapshot

per ADR 0014 -- supersedes ADR 0010's \`jaeha_not_advisor\`). Holds the

research taste distilled from a focused curious-interview series with
the

researcher (54 nodes / 79 edges, the \`scientist\` profile

installed at \`\<local-profile-install\>/\` per S8 G2).

Consulted at decision points only: websearch direction, batch planning
(per

stream), reanalysis probe selection, and gap/future-direction synthesis.

\> \*\*R5 mandate -- \`learn=False\` on every kkanbu call from
autoresearch

\> subagents.\*\* Session_id reuse within a single subagent invocation.
The

\> default \`learn=True\` would let autoresearch artifacts contaminate

\> kkanbu's identity model.

The per-stream flow is defined operationally by the subagent prompts in

\`subagents/\` and the state files in \`state/\` -- there is no separate

flowchart doc.

\## 7. Round5b: future ablation design (locked here for symmetry)

A separate later run, \*\*round5b\*\*, mirrors Round 5 with live kkanbu
replaced

by a \*\*static taste digest\*\* (ADR 0013). This design is locked
\*\*now\*\* so

Round 5 can be authored to be comparable to it.

\*\*Round5b configuration\*\*:

- Identical 11-stream / 4-batch parallel structure (no phases, per S4)

- Identical mandates (3-seed protocol, eval pipeline, immutables)

- Identical demo dataset

- Each kkanbu MCP call from a subagent is bypassed; instead, \*\*chunks
of

taste -- copied from the \`scientist\` kkanbu profile (the same
repo-frozen

snapshot R5 reads against, per ADR 0014) -- are pasted directly into the

R5b copies of the subagent prompt files\*\* as static text replacing the

live call. The same voice-framing prompt is replayed; only live,

per-decision graph retrieval is removed. (Which chunks / how much is

deliberately left loose -- see ADR 0013.) This paste-in is a
\*\*one-time

setup step done before R5b begins\*\* (analogous to R5's prerequisites,
S8) --

not part of the in-loop cycle.

- Same subagent roster; the digest reaches the 4 kkanbu-querying
subagents

(\`advisor-consult\`, \`websearcher\`, \`brainstormer\`,
\`mechanism-analyzer\`)

- Logged in \`\<ablation-run-root\>/\` (parallel directory tree)

The R5-vs-R5b comparison therefore holds the taste \*content\* constant
and

isolates \*\*live graph retrieval + grounding + calibration vs a static

digest of the same taste\*\*. R5's own subagents stay digest-free (they
rely

on live retrieval) -- this asymmetry is the measured quantity, stated

plainly in Appendix B. Which taste chunks to paste (selection / amount /

formatting) is deliberately left loose, deferred to R5b authoring; the

\*design\* is locked here. (The earlier "gated on cluster DB access"
caveat

is moot under ADR 0014 -- the canonical snapshot lives in the repo.)

Round5b is authored when Round 5 completes.

\## 8. Prerequisites (block stream launch)

Setup tasks must complete before the streams launch. \*\*They are done
\*outside\*

the 11-agent autoresearch loop\*\* -- typically by the
orchestrator-as-human, with

one-off scripts. They are setup work, not part of the in-loop experiment
cycle,

and not part of the round5b-reproducible spec. Per S11, this operational
detail

lives in \`resource/logistics/\`: the full runbook (commands, SQL prune
pattern,

halt conditions) is in \*\*\`resource/logistics/prerequisites.md\`\*\*.
There is no

required ordering among them; run \*\*G2 before C1\*\* so a broken-graph
halt is

caught before the expensive demo collection. (This list is the gating
\*rule\*;

per-item completion status is tracked in the runbook and \`state/\`
files, not

here. IDs were renumbered from P1-P7 to the C/G scheme on 2026-05-31 --
the

runbook holds the old-\>new map.)

Tasks split into \*\*Corrective\*\* (fixes for codebase-setup mistakes;
retired

once done, correct setup -\> CLAUDE.md) and \*\*Launch gates\*\*
(verify/decide/

operational; kept until launch):

- \*\*C1: Re-collect V5 demos\*\* -- single shared \`v5_clean.hdf5\` +
trajectory

conversion for the offline-RL and PIL streams (S12.3-12.5). \*\*Collect
at

k=3 (\`action_history_len=3\`, 75D) -- the MAX\*\*; every lower-k
dataset is

\*sliced\* from this bundle (S5), never re-collected. Do \*\*not\*\*
collect at

the k=1 default: you cannot slice up from a smaller bundle. (Enforced:

\`collect_demos_vmap.py\` raises if V5 collection runs at k!=3.)

- \*\*C2: V5 action-history unit test\*\* -- assert the raw pre-scaling
action is

stored in \`hierarchical_velocity_commands\` at the step it is taken.

- \*\*C3: Create missing V5 eval configs\*\* -- \`offline_rl\`,
\`pil_control\`,

\`pil_trajectory\`. \[DONE\] done (2026-05-31); retired -- see
CLAUDE.md.

- \*\*G1: Eval determinism check\*\* -- verify composite drift below
+/-0.3 pp (S2);

fix JAX/XLA determinism only if it exceeds.

- \*\*G2: Install and verify the \`scientist\` kkanbu profile\*\* --
copy the

repo-frozen snapshot into \`\<local-profile-install\>/knowledge.db\`,

confirm \`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\` reaches the MCP server, login, run a

\`kkanbu_answer\` LLM-tool ping. No R5-doc ingest (S3, S6; ADR 0010
carries

forward, ADR 0014 sets the profile). \*\*Halt branch\*\*: if install or
ping

fails irrecoverably, halt R5 and recover ad-hoc -- R5 does NOT degrade
to

a graph-less fallback (that would collapse R5 into R5b's static-digest
arm

and invalidate the comparison; ADR 0013).

- \*\*G3: Validate program.md\*\* -- internal consistency before
launching streams.

- \*\*G4: Launch the two crons\*\* (S6) -- nudge + maintainer; intervals
from

\`project.yaml crons\`. Up before the streams launch, down only when
Round 5

completes.

\## 9. Training and evaluation commands (reference)

\`\`\`bash

\# Activate env (always)

source activate.sh

\# PIL-Trajectory

python src/navigation/main.py train pil-trajectory \\

data/imitation/forest/v5_clean_trajectory.hdf5 \\

--horizon 10 --num-steps 150000

\# PIL-Control

python src/navigation/main.py train pil-control \\

data/imitation/forest/v5_clean.hdf5 \\

--num-steps 600000 --batch-size 1024 --learning-rate 1e-3 \\

--lr-schedule cosine --warmup-steps 1000

\# Offline RL (IQL example)

python src/navigation/main.py train iql \\

data/imitation/forest/v5_clean.hdf5 \\

--expectile 0.7 --temperature 3.0

\# Online RL (PPO) -- pure

JAX_SKIP_CUDA_CONSTRAINTS_CHECK=1 \\

python src/navigation/main.py train ppo \\

src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/pure_rl/training_config.py

\# Online RL -- privileged (asymmetric actor-critic)

python src/navigation/main.py train ppo \\

src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/privileged_rl/training_config.py

\# Density-sweep evaluation -- ONE unified path for every paradigm
(PIL/offline included)

python src/navigation/main.py evaluate \\

src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/\<stream\>/evaluation_config.py
\\

--checkpoint \<ckpt\> --output-dir \<dir\> --density-only

\# evaluator.py auto-derives action_history_len from the checkpoint; the
config carries

\# pil_mode/iql_mode/policy_type/trajectory_config. No standalone
harness, no --obs-mask.

\`\`\`

Full CLI reference: \`CLAUDE.md\`.

\*\*Main tree\*\* (\`\<repo-root\>/\`, branch \`main\`):

- \`\<run-root\>/experiment_cards/{stream}/batch\_{N}/\` -- every

experiment's card, partitioned by stream

- \`\<run-root\>/brainstormer/{stream}/batch\_{N}/\` -- per-stream-batch

brainstormer reports + iterations

- \`\<run-root\>/websearches/{stream}/batch\_{N}/\` -- per-stream-batch

websearch outputs

- \`\<run-root\>/state/{stream}/\` -- per-stream state files

- \`\<run-root\>/state/anchors/{stream}.json\` -- paradigm-stream

batch-1 anchor mean +/- CI (S2) per stream

(written by \`experiment-initial-analyzer\` for the 5 paradigm streams'
batch-1)

- \`\<run-root\>/state/{maintainer_report.md, budget.json, blocked.md}\`

- \`\<run-root\>/tools/\` -- shared analysis scripts

- \`\<run-root\>/worktrees/{stream}/B{N}-E1/\` -- experiment worktrees

- \`\<run-root\>/{program.md, project.yaml,

docs/adr/, resource/logistics/, subagents/}\` -- research spec

- \`data/\` (training data), \`example_data/locomotion/\` (frozen
checkpoint)

\*\*Worktrees\*\* (\`\<run-root\>/worktrees/{stream}/B{N}-E1/\`, each on

branch \`\<branch-prefix\>/exp-r5-{stream}-B{N}\` forked from
\`lite_round5\`):

- One per experiment. ~30 MB.

- Contains: \`src/\`, \`docs/\`,
\`experiment_for_paper/\*\*/\*.{sh,py,yaml,md}\`,

root config files, \`notes/\` (scratchpad).

- Does \*\*NOT\*\* contain: training data, \`example_data/\`, historical
outputs,

\`\<run-root\>/\` research spec, or any dynamic Round 5 dirs.

Agents reach those via absolute main-tree paths.

- Training and eval outputs go outside the worktree (cluster-specific
path);

never back into the worktree.

\*\*Per-stream slot count\*\*: only one slot per stream per batch in
Round 5

(unlike R4's 2 slots per stream). Each stream is one experiment per
batch.

That makes the card-id format \`{stream}-B{N}\` (no \`-E{S}\` suffix).

\## 11. Logistics hard constraints (summary)

These are absolute. Operational detail lives in \`subagents/\` and

\`resource/logistics/\`. Most are defined canonically elsewhere; this is

the single enforcement checklist:

- \*\*Identifiers\*\* (S10): card id \`{stream}-B{N}\` (e.g.,
\`pure_rl-B1\`,

\`d06-B2\`); branch \`\<branch-prefix\>/exp-r5-{stream}-B{N}\`. Training
data and the

locomotion checkpoint are referenced by absolute main-tree paths,

never copied into the worktree.

- \*\*GPU / SLURM resource requests are per-experiment, not fixed\*\*:
each

experiment chooses its GPU at submit time by \*\*live availability\*\*
per

\`resource/logistics/gpu_selection.md\` -- a typed gres is mandatory,
\*\*never

\`v100\`\*\*, the fast tier (\`nvidia_h200\`/\`h100\`/\`nvidia_l40s\`)
is preferred, and

\`p100\` is allowed but then the work must be \*\*small + parallel\*\*.
Size

\`--time\` from the maintainer's \`state/timing_ledger.json\` (empirical
durations

by stream / phase / \`gpu_type\`).

- \*\*No heavy commits back to \`lite_round5\`.\*\*

- \*\*No edits to \`program.md\`, \`project.yaml\`, ADRs, or subagent
prompts

by the loop.\*\* If a change is needed, write \`state/blocked.md\` and
halt.

- \*\*Per-stream parallel execution; batches sequential within a
stream\*\*

(S4.2-4.3). No phases, no cross-stream barrier (ADR 0012).

- \*\*kkanbu calls pass \`learn=False\`\*\* (S6); one \`session_id\` per

invocation, fresh across invocations.

- \*\*Subagent return validation.\*\* Every subagent returns

\`SUCCESS \| PARTIAL \| FAILURE\`; orchestrator advances only on
\`SUCCESS\`.

Max 2 retries per invocation.

- \*\*No R1-R4 findings seed Round 5 design\*\* (S3) -- numerical
anchors,

named leaders, finding lineages. Codebase improvements and methods are

exempt.

Per-stream batch advancement, state file semantics, retry rules,
debugger

skip conditions, and termination triggers are defined in S4.2-4.6 above
and

in the relevant subagent prompts (\`experiment-debugger.md\`,

\`maintainer.md\`).

\## 12. Paradigm conventions

\> Project-specific anchors per stream. Textbook content is
intentionally

\> omitted -- kkanbu and any vanilla-LLM round5b consumer have general
material

\> (PPO equations, IQL math, pure pursuit geometry) from pretraining.
What's

\> here is what you can't recover from web search: this project's
conventions,

\> file paths, default values, known issues, and the open questions
Round 5

\> tries to make progress on.

Cross-stream anchors (apply to every paradigm):

- \*\*Locomotion\*\*: frozen. Absolute path

\`\<frozen-locomotion-checkpoint\>\`.

- \*\*Core policy MLP\*\*: hidden sizes \`(512, 256, 128)\`, immutable.

- \*\*V5 observation\*\*: 2D goal (distance, heading) + 64D LIDAR
(single ring) +

\`3k\`D action history (\`k\` = \`action_history_len\`). The \*\*75D\*\*
form (k=3, 9D

history) is the max / canonical-data layout; \*\*R5 default is k=1 -\>
69D\*\*

(S5; H1 action-history ablation). Implementation:

\`src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/\`.

- \*\*Action space (RL & PIL-Control)\*\*: 3D body-frame velocity
\`(v_x, v_y, v_yaw)\`.

- \*\*LIDAR\*\*: 64 beams, 2D ring topology. Beam 63 is adjacent to beam
0.

- \*\*Density\*\*: training at \`delta = 0.04 trees/m^2\`; evaluation
across the six-density

sweep \`{0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16}\` weighted per S2.

\### 12.1 pure_rl (PPO)

- Default training config:
\`src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/pure_rl/training_config.py\`

- Default eval config:
\`src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/pure_rl/evaluation_config.py\`

- Reward weighting (from \`pure_rl/training_config.py\`):

 - \`collision = -10\` (project default; the \`-50\` value in older
notes was

the \`fall\` weight, not \`collision\`)

 - \`fall = -50\`, \`goal_reached = 250\`, \`goal_progress = 50\`,

\`goal_distance = -0.01\`, \`boundary = -0.5\`

 - \`velocity_smoothness = -1\`: kkanbu-tunable knob (streams 1-2 and
10-11)

- Training steps: ~15M

- Critic: symmetric (sees same obs as actor -- no privileged info)

- Action-history length: kkanbu-available knob \`action_history_len in
{0,1,2,3}\` (all streams; obs/network auto-adapt, no data regen). R5
default \*\*k=1\*\* (S5); may revert to k=3 if PPO jerkiness returns
(S13.6). Action-history length is a permitted knob; the batch-0 anchor
may differ in obs dim from later experiments.

\### 12.2 privileged_rl

- Default training config:
\`src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/privileged_rl/training_config.py\`

- Two sub-paradigms available:

 - \*\*Asymmetric actor-critic\*\*: critic sees \`privileged_state\`
(combined

state + normalized waypoints); actor sees LIDAR + state only. There is

no dedicated network file -- the asymmetry is implemented env-side: the

\`strategy="privileged_rl"\` switch in

\`src/navigation/envs/go1_navigation_forest_env_v5.py\` (search

\`privileged_state\`) exposes the extra state in \`info\`, and the
standard

PPO trainer wires the critic to read it. Config:

\`src/navigation/configs/Go1NavigationForestEnvV5/privileged_rl/training_config.py\`.

 - \*\*Privileged-obs distillation\*\*: privileged-obs teacher policy
-\>

LIDAR-only student via behavior cloning / DAgger. Pipeline lives in

\`src/navigation/imitation/bc_trainer/\`.

- Reward weighting inherited from \`pure_rl\` defaults unless the card
overrides.

- Action-history length: \`action_history_len\` (k in {0,1,2,3}) tunable
per S5 -- RL, obs/network auto-adapt, no data regen. Default
\*\*k=1\*\*; may revert to k=3 per S13.6. Action-history length is a
permitted knob; the batch-0 anchor may differ in obs dim from later
experiments.

\### 12.3 offline_rl

- \*\*Action space: 3D body-frame velocity \`(v_x, v_y, v_yaw)\` for
\*every\*

offline-RL algorithm\*\* (IQL, CQL, TD3+BC) -- same as \`pure_rl\` /
\`pil_control\`

(S12 cross-stream anchor). \*\*None output a trajectory.\*\* The

\`OfflineReplayBuffer\`'s \`trajectory_mode\` \*decodes\* waypoints -\>
velocity

(\`derive_velocities_from_trajectory\`; \`action_dim\` is always 3), so
loading a

trajectory HDF5 only changes the data source / reward shaping -- never
the

policy output. A waypoint-action offline-RL policy would need a new 20D
actor

 + Q/V and does not exist in this codebase.

- Available algorithms with trainers wired: \*\*IQL, CQL\*\*. TD3+BC has
actor/critic

network components in \`src/navigation/networks/\` but no end-to-end
trainer in

\`src/navigation/training/offline_rl/trainers/\`; AWR/AWAC are not
implemented.

A brainstormer slot proposing TD3+BC / AWR / AWAC must include the
trainer

wire-up in its experiment scope (and is subject to the S4.6 SLURM-ALGO
cap if

the wire-up keeps failing).

- Default hyperparameters per implemented algorithm:

 - IQL: \`expectile = 0.7\`, \`temperature = 3.0\`

 - CQL: \`cql_alpha = 1.0\`

- Demo dataset (shared with PIL streams):
\`data/imitation/forest/v5_clean.hdf5\`

(\>=10k success-filtered episodes at delta=0.04, success-only -- see S8
prereq C1).

The expert's safety margin around obstacles is set at scenario-gen time
via

\`boundary_safety_margin = 0.5 m\`, matching the value used in every V5
RL

training config so the planned paths embed the same safety boundary the
RL

envs penalize. (There is no separate \`obstacle_inflation\` knob in this

codebase -- A\* receives the same clearance as the env's collision
model.)

- Reward shaping: computed from observations at training time

(\`sparse_goal(+10) + dense_distance_shaping + collision_penalty\`).

- Known constraint (R4 lesson, kept for context): expert-only demos
limit

what offline RL can learn beyond BC. Streams attempting offline RL
should

consider hybrid offline-\>online or data-augmentation variants if pure

offline plateaus.

- Implementations:
\`src/navigation/training/offline_rl/trainers/{iql_trainer,cql_trainer}.py\`

(sharing \`base_offline_rl_trainer.py\`).

- Action-history length: \`action_history_len\` (k in {0,1,2,3}) tunable
per S5 --

default \*\*k=1\*\* (H1 ablation). Datasets for any k \<= 3

are \*\*sliced from the canonical k=3 / 75D bundle (no
re-collection)\*\*; the net

input layer auto-adapts. Action-history length is a permitted knob; the
batch-0

anchor may differ in obs dim from later experiments.

- \*\*Core-MLP deviation (batch-0 anchor only -- known TODO):\*\* the
\`offline_rl\` B0

anchor was trained as a \`LIDARAttentionGaussianActor\` with
actor/critic width

\`\[256,256\]\` + attention, NOT the \`(512,256,128)\` core. This is a
pre-launch

expedient (no time to re-train before launch). The \`(512,256,128)\`
core-MLP

constraint (S5) remains \*\*non-negotiable for every batch-1+
autoresearch

experiment\*\*; a batch-1+ \`offline_rl\` slot should bring the policy
onto the

standard core (the attention block may be treated as an auxiliary module
around

it). See the \`offline_rl-B0\` card's \`7\_gap_and_future\`.

\### 12.4 pil_control (PIL -- velocity action)

- Action space: 3D velocity directly (Behavior Cloning on \`(75D_obs,
3D_vel)\` pairs)

- Network: \`StudentPolicyNetwork\` (75D -\> core MLP -\> 3D output)

in \`src/navigation/networks/student_policy_network.py\`. (Older notes
call

this \`VelocityPolicyNetwork\`; the class is named
\`StudentPolicyNetwork\` in

the current source.)

- Default config: \`src/navigation/configs/pil_forest_config.py\`

- Demo dataset: \`data/imitation/forest/v5_clean.hdf5\`

- Default training hyperparameters:

 - 600k steps, batch 1024, learning rate 1e-3, cosine schedule, 1000
warmup steps

- Action-history length: \`action_history_len\` (k in {0,1,2,3}) tunable
per S5 --

default \*\*k=1\*\* (H1 ablation: best success+smoothness for BC
control). Datasets

for any k \<= 3 are \*\*sliced from the canonical k=3 / 75D bundle (no

re-collection)\*\*; \`StudentPolicyNetwork\`'s input layer auto-adapts.
Action-history

length is a permitted knob; the batch-0 anchor may differ in obs dim
from later

experiments.

\> Note: the batch-0 anchor is evaluated from a V3-env-trained
checkpoint (66D), retained as a provisional number-to-beat; it will be
replaced by a V5 6-density re-eval (see state/batch0_vpn_queue.md). The
env immutable (S5) still binds all Round-5 experiments.

\### 12.5 pil_trajectory (PIL -- waypoint action)

- Action space: 10 waypoints \`\[x1, y1, ..., x10, y10\]\`,
\`trajectory_scale = 5.0\` (meters).

\`trajectory_scale\` is the per-axis waypoint reach ceiling: the network
output is

\`tanh(\*) \* trajectory_scale\`, so each coordinate is bounded to
+/-\`trajectory_scale\` m.

It MUST be \>= the reach of the (un-normalized, meter-valued) horizon-10
targets, or

far waypoints clip -- do not lower it without re-deriving the target
magnitudes. The

training/eval invariant is pinned at 5.0
(\`src/navigation/configs/pil_forest_trajectory_config.py\`).

- Pure-pursuit conversion: waypoints -\> 3D velocity command at runtime

 - \`lookahead_index\`: which waypoint Pure Pursuit chases
(kkanbu-tunable)

- Network: \`TrajectoryPolicyNetwork\` (75D -\> core MLP -\> 20-dim
waypoint output)

in \`src/navigation/networks/student_policy_network.py\`

- Demo dataset: \`data/imitation/forest/v5_clean_trajectory.hdf5\`

(converted from \`v5_clean.hdf5\` via

\`src/navigation/imitation/forest/convert_to_trajectory_dataset_from_positions.py
--horizon 10\`)

- Default training hyperparameters: 150k steps, \`horizon = 10\`

- Action-history length: \`action_history_len\` (k in {0,1,2,3}) tunable
per S5 --

default \*\*k=1\*\*. Datasets for any k \<= 3 are \*\*sliced from the
canonical k=3 /

75D bundle (no re-collection)\*\*; \`TrajectoryPolicyNetwork\`'s input
layer

auto-adapts. Action-history length is a permitted knob; the batch-0
anchor may

differ in obs dim from later experiments.

\> Note: the batch-0 anchor is evaluated from a V3-env-trained
checkpoint (66D), retained as a provisional number-to-beat; it will be
replaced by a V5 6-density re-eval (see state/batch0_vpn_queue.md). The
env immutable (S5) still binds all Round-5 experiments.

- \*\*MAF (min_alignment_factor)\*\*: low-level controller parameter
affecting

forward-motion commitment. Historically \`0.3\` acted as an implicit
symmetry-breaker

for memoryless policies in dense forests. The 3-step action history (V5
default)

is the principled fix; MAF is no longer load-bearing but remains a
tunable.

- \*\*Known issue (carried into R5)\*\*: trajectory-mode currently
underperforms

velocity-mode (~0% success rate at high densities) despite the
theoretical

advantages of waypoint actions. This is one of the open questions Round
5

is structured to make progress on -- \`pil_trajectory\` slots should be

designed with this finding as the context, not a presumed property.

\### 12.6 d06-d09 (kkanbu-led exploration)

- \*\*d06-d07\*\*: combination / improvement of the paradigm streams.

Cross-paradigm hybrids (e.g., offline-\>online), architectural
extensions on

top of a paradigm result, or transfer of a paradigm mechanism to another

paradigm. Kkanbu picks freely. Because streams run in parallel (S4.2),

batch-1 designs from paradigm \*priors\* (blind to siblings); batches
2-4

fold in whatever sibling results have completed.

- \*\*d08-d09\*\*: totally new ideas outside the 5 paradigm streams.

Candidate territories: world models (DreamerV3 family), transformer
policy

backbones, generative obstacle prediction as auxiliary task,

episode-50 universal-failure mitigations. d08-d09 slots

are \*\*anchorless\*\* (\`card.anchor_reference = null\`); the bar is
the

card's \`expected_falsification\` clause, not a paradigm anchor. The

mechanical cratered gate of S4.4 governs seed-2+3 launch -- including

the "hypothesis falsified at single-seed level" clause that lets a

paradigm-discovery slot stop at seed 1 without ad-hoc orchestrator

discretion.

\### 12.7 d10-d11 (tuning within constraint)

- Per S5 "Tuning defined by negation":

"No new losses, no new paradigms, no architectural changes. Network core

immutable. Any other hyperparameter is fair."

- \*\*Batch-1\*\* tunes a \*\*fixed baseline paradigm assigned
upfront\*\* by the

brainstormer (a runnable default config in \`src/navigation\`, e.g.

\`pure_rl/training_config.py\` or the IQL CLI defaults) -- so d10/d11
run in

parallel from t=0 without waiting for any experiment (ADR 0012).

- \*\*Later batches re-target the current champion\*\* = the
highest-composite

\`complete\` card across all streams at brainstorm time (read from the

maintainer's \`index.md\`). Tuning still touches only hyperparameters,
so any

champion -- including a d08/d09 exotic -- is a legal target (grind its

hyperparameters, not its architecture). Streams 10 and 11 may share a

target or diverge.

- Eval pipeline immutability applies here too (S5) -- d10-d11 has no

carveout to "fix" eval bugs locally. Suspected eval bugs halt the loop

per S8 (escalates to orchestrator-as-human for an autoresearch restart).

\### 12.8 Architecture conventions (apply across all paradigms)

The LIDAR architecture family the project considers, with the structural

inductive biases each respects (per program.md S5: only auxiliary
modules

around the immutable core MLP are free):

- \*\*MLP\*\* (flat 64-dim input): respects no LIDAR symmetries;
baseline.

- \*\*Circular CNN\*\*: shift-equivariant on the ring (beam 63 \<-\>
beam 0).

- \*\*PointNet\*\* (set view): permutation-invariant; density-invariant
by construction.

- \*\*Attention\*\* (LIDAR-Attention): empirically strongest baseline at
narrow

density gaps; relies on learned bias rather than structural invariance.

- \*\*PointNet++\*\*: hierarchical set abstraction -- partially in scope
if

d08-d09 explores it.

Specifying a non-default LIDAR architecture is a kkanbu-available design

decision in any stream's slot proposal (assuming it doesn't violate the

core-MLP immutability -- auxiliary perception heads around the core are
free).

\## 13. Project overview

\> Distilled from R4's \`about_playground_test.md\`.

\> This section is what kkanbu and any round5b vanilla-LLM consumer need

\> to ground themselves in the codebase's domain, philosophy, and

\> conventions. R4-specific numbers and named leaders are intentionally

\> omitted per S3 -- R5 establishes its own anchors (human-seeded batch
0 where provided, else batch-1).

\### 13.1 The one question the repo is trying to answer

\> \*\*How do we get a neural-network policy to do the right thing in

\> situations it has never seen, instead of memorizing the training

\> conditions?\*\*

The hard part of training a policy is not getting it to perform on its

training distribution -- neural networks overfit by default. The hard

part is producing a policy whose behavior makes sense \*outside\* that

distribution. The project's word for this is \*\*generalizability\*\*.

This is not a benchmark-chasing project. The goal is not the highest

absolute number. The goal is \*\*the smallest gap between
in-distribution

and out-of-distribution performance\*\*, on a distribution shift that

actually matters. Everything else (observation design, network

architecture, training paradigm, evaluation weighting) is in service of

answering that question with rigor.

\### 13.2 The concrete testbed

- \*\*Robot\*\*: \*\*Unitree Go1\*\*, a quadruped with 12 joint motors

(hip / knee / ankle x 4 legs). Simulated in \*\*MuJoCo\*\* via the

\*\*MuJoCo Playground / Brax\*\* JAX framework.

- \*\*Perception\*\*: \*\*LIDAR\*\* only -- a ring of 64 distance beams
(each

normalized 0=close, 1=far). No camera, no depth image. Sim-to-real

is explicitly out of scope (S5).

- \*\*Goal\*\*: navigate from a start pose to a goal pose in a room full

of static cylindrical "trees." Trees don't move; no dynamic

obstacles.

- \*\*Room\*\*: 30 x 30 m (immutable in R5).

- \*\*Hierarchy\*\*: the policy is split into two layers.

 - \*\*Locomotion layer\*\*: takes a 3D velocity command, outputs 12
joint

torques. Pre-trained (~100M PPO steps on flat terrain) and frozen.

No navigation experiment touches it.

 - \*\*Navigation layer\*\*: reads V5 75D observation

(2D goal + 64D LIDAR + 9D action history), outputs either a 3D

velocity (\`pil_control\`, RL paradigms) or a 10-waypoint trajectory

(\`pil_trajectory\`). \*\*This is the only layer the project trains.\*\*

Walking is treated as a solved engineering problem. All research

capacity focuses on the decision-making layer -- route choices -- where

generalization actually matters.

\### 13.3 Why density?

\*\*Density\*\* = trees per square metre. Low density = sparse forest =

easy. High density = packed = hard.

The project trains policies at one fixed density (\*\*delta = 0.04

trees/m^2\*\*) and evaluates across \*\*six densities\*\*

\`{0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16}\` -- a 16x range from sparsest to

densest, with training at the middle.

Density was chosen as the OOD axis after also studying obstacle shape

and size. Shape and size drops were 4-9 percentage points of success

at worst. Density caused a much larger drop. Studying a small effect

teaches nothing; studying the effect that dominates is where

understanding becomes possible.

The composite score (S2) weights high densities more heavily

(2.5x at delta=0.16 vs 1.0x at training). This is \*\*deliberate metric

design\*\*: it says "I care more about surviving at 4x training density

than about perfection at training density." The metric is itself an

expression of the research stance.

\### 13.4 V5 observation: the result of subtractive design

The navigation policy's input has gone through several generations of

\*\*simplification\*\* (V1 -\> V5). Each revision \*removed\* features
rather

than adding them:

- \*\*V1\*\*: absolute \`(x, y)\` position in the room, dense goal
encoding.

Memorized coordinates; failed when room dimensions changed.

- \*\*V2\*\*: removed absolute position; kept rich goal encoding.

- \*\*V3\*\*: reduced goal encoding to 2D (distance + heading),
normalized

by room diagonal. 66D total.

- \*\*V4\*\*: minor refinement.

- \*\*V5\*\* (the R5 standard): 2D goal + 64D LIDAR + \`3k\`D action
history.

Action history was added specifically to fix the perceptual-symmetry /

decision-stability problem (S13.6); the original fix used 3 timesteps

(75D). The H1 ablation later found a \*\*single\*\*

most-recent action (k=1, 69D) gives the best success/smoothness tradeoff

on BC, so \*\*R5 defaults to k=1\*\* while k=3 remains available (S5).

The philosophy: \*\*richer observations invite more overfitting\*\*. If
a

dimension isn't earning its keep as a scale-invariant,

generalization-friendly signal, it should be removed.

A live tension the project takes seriously: a cleaner observation is

not automatically a more generalizable one. Some OOD axes are

better-served by \*some\* redundancy in the goal signal. The subtractive

trajectory is not religion; it's a strong prior with documented

exceptions.

\### 13.5 The space of methods (cross-paradigm comparison)

The project is deliberately \*\*multi-paradigm\*\*. Rather than tuning
one

method to death, R5 compares whole families on the same density-sweep:

- \*\*Imitation Learning (PIL)\*\* -- a privileged-information expert

(A\\ planner + Pure Pursuit) generates demos; a LIDAR-only student

is trained to reproduce them. Two sub-variants: PIL-Control (3D

velocity output) and PIL-Trajectory (10-waypoint output + Pure

Pursuit controller). See S12.4-12.5 for project conventions.

- \*\*Offline Reinforcement Learning\*\* -- same expert data, fed
through

IQL / CQL / TD3+BC / AWR. Known limitation: expert-only data

constrains what value-based methods can learn beyond BC (S12.3).

- \*\*Online Reinforcement Learning (PPO)\*\* -- no demonstrations; the

policy learns by trying, colliding, getting punished. Symmetric or

asymmetric variants (privileged critic). See S12.1-12.2.

Architectures for the LIDAR perception layer (around the immutable

core MLP) include MLP baseline, Circular CNN, PointNet (set view,

density-invariant by construction), PointNet++, and Attention. See

S12.8.

Why multi-paradigm: any single paradigm's OOD result could be a quirk

of its loss surface. The cross-paradigm pattern is what survives. If

all paradigms converge to roughly the same OOD ceiling, that ceiling

is a property of the task formulation -- and finding it (then breaking

it by changing the formulation rather than the method) is one of the

highest-value possible Round 5 outcomes.

\### 13.6 The MAF / oscillation case study (carried into R5 as context)

This is the project's worked example of \*\*how diagnosis beats variant

sweeping\*\*. R5 inherits the diagnosis as context; the underlying

question (decision stability under perceptual symmetry) remains live.

\*\*Setup\*\*: PIL-Trajectory outputs waypoints; Pure Pursuit converts

them to velocity. Pure Pursuit has a parameter MAF

(\`min_alignment_factor\`) -- the minimum forward speed the robot

maintains regardless of heading misalignment.

\*\*Failure mode at MAF=0 in dense forests\*\*: the robot stops to
rotate

when facing away from the lookahead point, but its LIDAR doesn't

change while stationary, so the policy re-computes the same ambiguous

decision and flips. Result: vyaw oscillates between extremes, no

forward progress, timeout.

\*\*Three interacting causes\*\*:

1. In dense forests, left-path and right-path are often
\*\*symmetric\*\*

-- equally viable from the agent's perspective.

2. The policy is \*\*memoryless\*\* (V3 obs had no history). Every

timestep is an independent decision.

3. MAF=0 lets the robot stop. With no forward motion, the LIDAR

reading barely changes, so the decision input doesn't change, so

the decision flips with noise.

MAF=0.3 had previously hidden the bug by forcing forward drift, which

broke symmetry by changing the robot's position. The forced motion

was acting as an \*\*implicit commitment mechanism\*\*, not just a

smoothness prior.

\*\*The fix that worked\*\*: 3-step action history appended to the

observation (V3 66D -\> V5 75D). The policy now sees its last 3 velocity

commands, can detect "I've been turning left," and commits to its prior

choice rather than flipping. This is the principled fix; MAF is no

longer load-bearing but remains a tunable. (The \*amount\* of history is

itself a knob -- the later H1 ablation found a

single most-recent action \`k=1\` recovers the smoothing effect at the

best success/smoothness tradeoff, so R5 defaults to k=1 (S5); the 3-step

form remains the fallback if PPO jerkiness returns.)

\*\*Why this matters for R5\*\*: the V5 standard inherits this fix. Slot

proposals (especially in \`pil_trajectory\`, \`d06\`-\`d09\`) should
treat

"perceptual symmetry resolution" as a solved-but-instrumented problem

-- not a presumed property to ignore, but also not the central

mechanism to re-investigate without specific reason.

\### 13.7 The researcher's stance

Six principles that thread through the codebase:

1. \*\*Overfitting is the null hypothesis.\*\* Generalization is work,
not

default. The metric weighting (S2) is calibrated to punish OOD

failure more than it rewards in-distribution success.

2. \*\*Remove features before adding them.\*\* Subtractive observation

design (V1-\>V5). A dimension that doesn't do scale-invariant work

is a liability.

3. \*\*Prefer inductive biases symmetric with the world.\*\*
Architectures

like PointNet and circular CNN encode structural priors that

reflect the world's actual symmetries (LIDAR rotational

equivariance, density invariance) rather than learning them.

4. \*\*A failure mode well-diagnosed \> a marginal gain well-tuned.\*\*
The

MAF/oscillation story (S13.6) is the template. A hypothesis, a

measurement, a root cause, a minimal fix, a quantitative

improvement.

5. \*\*Be honest about what you don't understand.\*\* Mechanism claims
for

\*why\* PointNet beats MLP, \*why\* attention helps, \*why\* trajectory

underperforms velocity, remain hypothesized. Open edges, not solved

problems.

6. \*\*Rigor comes from volume and structure.\*\* Multi-seed protocol,

composite-score weighting, paradigm-self-calibrating anchors,

stratified percentile bootstrap CIs (S2, S4.4-4.5). A claim is not

a claim until the evidence is at this scale.

\### 13.8 What is NOT in scope

(Restated from S5 for the kkanbu / round5b reader who lands here first:)

- \*\*Sim-to-real transfer.\*\* Studied; depth cameras would 10x
training

cost with no obvious generalization benefit. Deferred. LIDAR is the

committed input modality.

- \*\*Dynamic obstacles.\*\* Trees are static.

- \*\*Locomotion research.\*\* Walking layer frozen.

- \*\*Leaderboard hunting.\*\* Round 5 would rather understand \*why\* a

method works than push it 0.5% higher.
````
